title: Thiriet by TDS wins at Red Bull Ring after a day of headlight trouble
dek: Pierre Thiriet, Mathias Beche and Ryo Hirakawa won the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring in the #46 Oreca, 51 seconds clear of Eurasia, after pole-sitter Panis Barthez and G-Drive both lost the lead.

chapters.title: A thinner grid and a few late changes
text: The 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 17 July 2016 was the third round of the European Le Mans Series, and the first race since the Le Mans 24 Hours had interrupted the season. So24! by Lombard Racing, third at Silverstone in April with its Ligier, filed for bankruptcy on 5 July and withdrew from the championship, leaving the LMP2 field a car short for the trip to Styria.

Elsewhere the entry list shuffled. Nathanael Berthon had replaced Kuba Giermaziak in the Greaves Motorsport Ligier #41 at Le Mans, and the team confirmed him for the rest of the season, alongside Memo Rojas and Julien Canal. Murphy Prototypes brought back Karun Chandhok for the Oreca 03R #48, joined by Guglielmo Belotti and Sean Doyle, while its new Ave-Riley AR-2 stayed away and was pencilled in for a later debut. Algarve Pro Racing used the days before the race to test at the circuit, with Andrea Pizzitola and Jonathan Hirschi joining team owner Michael Munemann in the #25 Ligier.

The series also staged its first separate Bronze test, an answer to the poor driving standards seen at Imola, and Munemann led it in the Algarve Ligier. In practice G-Drive Racing's Harry Tincknell set the pace on Friday in the Gibson 015S #38 before an off in the closing minutes damaged the left side of the car, and Thiriet by TDS Racing topped Saturday morning's session, 0.026 seconds ahead of Nicolas Lapierre's DragonSpeed Oreca.

chapters.title: Panis Barthez takes pole by five hundredths
text: Paul Loup Chatin put the Panis Barthez Competition Ligier #23 on pole with a 1:20.700 in the final minutes, after raising the benchmark to 1:20.720 with just over three minutes left. The team's pole in LMP2 was matched by another in LMP3, so the squad swept both prototype classes. Chatin said he would not start the car himself, as Timothe Buret was down to take the green flag.

The top five were covered by roughly a quarter of a second. Mathias Beche was second in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca #46 on 1:20.753, only 0.053 seconds off pole, and Tincknell set 1:20.826 for third in the G-Drive Gibson #38 after trading fastest laps with Beche early in the session. Tristan Gommendy took fourth for Eurasia Motorsport with a lap in the final minutes, and Lapierre was fifth for DragonSpeed even after spinning on his last flying lap, 0.256 seconds from pole.

Olivier Pla (Krohn Racing), Pizzitola (Algarve Pro) and Julian Leal (SMP Racing) filled the next three places on the grid, with Greaves ninth, Murphy tenth and the Pegasus Morgan eleventh at the back of the class.

chapters.title: Buret streaks away, then everything goes wrong
text: Buret made the best start and pulled clear of the field, while Giedo van der Garde climbed from third to second in the G-Drive car. The scrap with Gommendy in the early corners left the Gibson with a front-left slow puncture and a trip to the pits that dropped it to ninth. Gommendy moved up to second, with Lapierre next and Pierre Thiriet settling in fourth after what he called a bad start.

Gommendy stayed on the leader's tail through traffic, but the lead changed hands when Buret clipped the GTE-leading JMW Ferrari through the final corner on lap 27. The contact left the Ligier fourth, and Buret then served a drive-through penalty for an incorrect starting formation before running off at Turn 6. That first stint was the start of a day of trouble for the pole-sitting car.

Eurasia's #33 and DragonSpeed's #21 were first to make their driver changes, with Pu Junjin taking over from Gommendy and Henrik Hedman from Lapierre. Van der Garde, meanwhile, drove at a furious pace to regain the lost time and led briefly as others stopped. By the hour mark Thiriet, Pu and Hedman held the first three positions.

chapters.title: The first headlight repair
text: G-Drive made its regular change just under an hour in, with Simon Dolan taking over and rejoining sixth. Thiriet held a 25-second lead over Pu until, around halfway through the second hour, the headlight cluster of the TDS Oreca failed and it was brought in. Ryo Hirakawa took over, and the replacement nose was finished in the blue and white of KCMG, giving the winner a hybrid look for a few hours.

The stop dropped the car to fourth, but the order reshuffled as the others pitted. Hirakawa led again from Leal's SMP Racing BR 01 #32, with Dolan third and Nico Pieter de Bruijn fourth in the Eurasia car, ahead of Canal in the Greaves Ligier. A Full Course Yellow came about fifteen minutes before half-distance for a stranded car in the gravel at Turn 5, and shortly after the halfway point de Bruijn passed Dolan for third.

chapters.title: Beche takes over, DragonSpeed falls away
text: Hirakawa kept the gap to second-placed Leal at about 25 seconds until both stopped on the same lap with roughly 90 minutes left. Beche took the TDS Oreca, Stefano Coletti the SMP car, and Tincknell climbed into the G-Drive Gibson for the run to the flag, about 30 seconds off the lead. Coletti spun after getting involved with two lapped cars at the last corner but still had about 15 seconds in hand over the Gibson.

The DragonSpeed Oreca #21, an early contender, hit the barrier leaving the pits and suffered a rear-left suspension failure. Ben Hanley limped round a full lap to get it back, but the damage was terminal and the car was not classified with 103 laps. Krohn Racing's Ligier #40, which would be beached late on, finished a distant 32nd.

chapters.title: Tincknell's podium chance ends at Turn 2
text: Tincknell took third from Coletti early in the final hour, as the SMP car faced an unscheduled stop for faulty rear lights caused by loose bodywork, and then passed de Bruijn at Turn 2 for second just as the TDS Oreca made its final stop. Pierre Thiriet got back in the car and had the front clip replaced for a second time because the headlight of the replacement piece had worked loose, this time returning in the correct TDS colours.

The race changed again with 40 minutes left. Tincknell had made his last fuel stop and rejoined, only to be hit at Turn 2 by Remy Striebig's Pegasus Racing Morgan #29, which was several laps down and had spun on the exit of the corner. The collision wrecked the front-left corner of the Gibson, forcing another visit to the pits for bodywork under the Full Course Yellow. Tincknell called the incident terrible driving and said he had been on for second place before he had to nurse the car home.

That let Gommendy back into second and moved Thiriet into the lead for good. A third Full Course Yellow in the last ten minutes, to recover Tracy Krohn's beached Ligier, left the order unchanged. Thiriet by TDS Racing won on 160 laps, 51.622 seconds ahead of the Eurasia Oreca of Pu, de Bruijn and Gommendy. G-Drive was third a further 7.5 seconds back and set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:22.392 from van der Garde.

Coletti's SMP BR 01 was fourth, a lap down, after its bodywork issues, and Pizzitola passed Rojas on the final lap to give Algarve Pro fifth, the best of the Ligier JS P2 entries. Greaves was sixth. Panis Barthez finished seventh, Chatin bringing the pole-sitter home after Buret's first-stint problems, one lap down. Murphy was eighth, four laps behind the winner.

chapters.title: A first ELMS podium for Eurasia and a tighter title race
text: Beche said it felt like his first ELMS race of the year, having missed Silverstone and driven only a few laps at Imola, and that the new setup had given the car great balance all weekend. Thiriet joked that he must have been asleep at the start, but said the pace was fine after that. For a car that spent the day with a loose headlight and a borrowed nose, it was a win built on quick pit work and consistent pace.

Gommendy said it was Eurasia Motorsport's first time on the ELMS podium, and that the team had held back at Le Mans and in earlier races to build mileage but could push from the start in Austria. Pu was convinced there was more to come, as both he and de Bruijn felt they could manage their tyres better in their stints.

G-Drive left with the consolation of third place and the fastest lap. Van der Garde explained that the early puncture probably came from a broken valve in his fight with Gommendy, after which he was pushing flat out. Tincknell said that he had been on for second, and that the contact with Pegasus left the car vibrating and porpoising so badly that he could only bring it home. For Panis Barthez, the pole-sitter's afternoon of a drive-through, a clash with the JMW Ferrari and a faulty headlight ended in seventh place.
The result moved Thiriet by TDS Racing to within eight points of G-Drive's championship lead in LMP2. The next round was the 4 Hours of Le Castellet at Paul Ricard on 28 August.

facts.v: The #46 Oreca won on 160 laps, 51.622 seconds ahead of Eurasia, despite two unscheduled stops for a faulty headlight.
